newsitem.title: UK: Hard Rock Cafe operator Rank posts lower profits.
newsitem.headline: Hard Rock Cafe operator Rank posts lower profits.

text.p: Britain's Rank Group Plc, which operates Hard Rock Cafes around the world, Thursday posted sharply lower profits for 1996 but said its outlook was good and unveiled plans for 3,000 new jobs.

Profits before tax in 1996 fell to 65 million pounds ($105.1 million) from 515 million pounds ($832.8 million) for the previous year. Profits in 1996 were dragged lower by a charge of 232 million pounds ($375 million) for property writedowns and restructuring charges, while 1995 results were boosted by a one-time gain of 236 million pounds ($381.6 million).

Rank said it will create 3,000 full-time jobs in Britain this year as part of a radical restructuring. The jobs will be in new bingo clubs, pub-restaurants, nightclubs, cinemas, resorts and a new leisure centre.
In the past year Rank has completed a financial restructuring and decided to focus on four areas -- Hard Rock, Holidays, Leisure and Film and Entertainment Services.
"These changes, together with the benefits of our investment programme and the generally favourable economic climate, provide a promising outlook for Rank," Chief Executive Andrew Teare said.

He said Rank plans to sell its film distribution unit, which has a catalogue of films, a British distribution joint venture with U.S.-based Castle Rock-Turner and an international sales arm. Press reports have speculated the sale might raise up to 150 million pounds ($242.6 million).
Operating profit at three of Rank's four core divisions showed double-figure growth. Profits at Holidays fell 1 percent as margins came under pressure in its U.S. operations.
